newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 up at 41.45 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday amid higher supplies and low buying of the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee is likely to open stable on Tuesday, a dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rupee rate, last changed on May 23, was 40.3900/40.5920 against the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.60 percent compared to the opening at 2.70 percent.
